critiques.assumption: A matching silhouette kit and ordered-layout drawing establish that the actual accepted order is complete and correctly represented.
critiques.limitation: If both inherit the same wrong layout mapping, they can agree while omitting a required partition. Neither such an error nor silhouette ambiguity is observed in the supplied case. A1's proposal does not explicitly require an order-source check independent of the spatial mapping; Z1 already proposes independent reconciliation.
critiques.opening: Retain spatial guidance but validate its mapping against the accepted order before reusing it, and reconcile each packed kit against that order.
critiques.comparison: Z1 supplies an independent completeness check but does not itself resolve customer placement; Z2 resolves placement only with correct contents and mapping. A1 combines spatial checking and interpretation. Adding Z1's independent reconciliation to A1 could interrupt shared mapping errors. The interaction is error containment across workshop and customer guidance; it fails if the checker merely copies the same mapping or its extra work defeats the time target.
critiques.probe: Proposed only: create sample kits containing correct parts, one omission, one substitution, and a deliberately wrong shared layout mapping. Compare A1 alone with A1 plus reconciliation against the accepted-order specification. Record detected discrepancies and all preparation/checking time. No physical tests have been performed.

openings.claim: Independent order reconciliation may make A1's shared spatial guidance robust to internally consistent mapping mistakes.
openings.delta: Validate each layout template against the accepted specification, then separately confirm packed component identities, counts and exterior color; retain the matching customer drawing.
openings.prediction: Compared with A1 alone, deliberately wrong shared mappings are caught more often. Compared with Z1 alone, the specific drawing may reduce customer placement errors. Both gains remain untested.
openings.probe: Reuse at most six sample sets for the discrepancy challenge across both workers. If feasible, use ten participants once each to compare verified kits with generic versus specific diagrams. Small trials assess mechanisms only; assess all three original success measures in the 60-unit pilot.
openings.fit: Conditional on measured feasibility within the original outcome and constraints.
assumptions: Accepted orders identify required components independently of the proposed mapping.
One bench, fifteen samples, 500 initial spending, 0.40 recurring increase and the fixed delivery date cover all work.
Footprint, assortment, removability, accepted counts and colors remain intact.
